question: Which anonymous report provides the stronger evidence-bounded bibliometric synthesis in coverage, explanation, structure, caution, and overall usefulness?

candidate_a:
# Anonymous Bibliometric Report

## Structured Abstract

**Background:** The intersection of extracellular vesicle (EV) biology and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing represents a rapidly emerging frontier in therapeutic delivery. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric mapping of the research landscape at this convergence.

**Methods:** A corpus of 259 unique publications (2015–2022) was acquired through deterministic, exhaustive retrieval and analyzed using performance indicators, science mapping, and network analysis. Bradford zoning, keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, and co-citation networks were constructed using association-strength normalization and Louvain community detection.

**Results:** The field exhibits explosive growth with a compound annual growth rate of 66.85%, peaking at 72 publications in 2022. The citation distribution is highly skewed (mean 72.09, median 32.00), with 13.51% of works remaining uncited. The intellectual structure reveals a dominant cluster centered on EV-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 delivery for cancer therapy, supported by foundational works on exosome engineering and RNA loading strategies. The social structure is characterized by a prominent Chinese research network anchored by Xiaohui Chen (14 publications) and institutional hubs including Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University. The conceptual structure, mapped through keyword co-occurrence, identifies five thematic clusters spanning fundamental EV biology, gene editing tools, cancer applications, analytical detection methods, and therapeutic engineering.

**Conclusions:** The research domain is transitioning from foundational EV characterization toward translational applications in gene therapy, with CRISPR/Cas9 delivery emerging as the central integrating theme. The concentration of highly cited works in recent years, combined with sustained growth, suggests an accelerating trajectory toward clinical relevance.

## Introduction

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as promising biological delivery vehicles for therapeutic macromolecules, offering advantages of biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and intrinsic targeting capabilities. Concurrently, the development of CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing technology has created unprecedented opportunities for treating genetic diseases, yet its clinical translation remains constrained by delivery challenges. The convergence of these two fields represents a rapidly evolving research frontier where EVs are being engineered to encapsulate and deliver CRISPR/Cas9 components to target cells.

Understanding the structure and dynamics of this interdisciplinary domain requires systematic bibliometric analysis that moves beyond simple metric reporting toward integrated interpretation of performance, social, conceptual, and intellectual structures. This study applies established bibliometric methods [E067][E068] to map the research landscape at the intersection of extracellular vesicles and CRISPR/Cas9 delivery, examining publication trends, citation impacts, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution.

## Methods

### Data Acquisition and Corpus Construction

A systematic search was conducted to identify publications at the intersection of extracellular vesicle research and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. The retrieval process employed cursor pagination continued until the source returned no next cursor, ensuring complete acquisition [E002]. The source reported 259 results, and 259 unique source records were acquired, confirming exhaustive coverage [E002]. After deterministic exact deduplication, the final canonical corpus contained 259 unique works [E001].

### Data Quality Assessment

Metadata completeness was evaluated across all canonical works. Critical fields demonstrated high coverage: publication date, document type, title, cited-by count, reference count, and source identifier were present for 100% of records [E003]. Abstract coverage reached 84.56% (219 of 259 works), while DOI coverage was 97.3% (252 of 259 works) [E003]. Language metadata was available for 99.61% of works [E003]. These coverage rates support robust bibliometric analysis while acknowledging that abstract-level analysis cannot substitute for full-text inspection [E027–E050].

### Analytical Framework

The analytical framework followed established bibliometric guidelines [E067] and science mapping methodologies [E068][E069]. Performance analysis examined publication output, citation distributions, and productivity rankings. Science mapping employed network construction using association-strength normalization (c_ij / (w_i * w_j)) with Louvain community detection [E070] for co-authorship, institution collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and co-citation networks.

Network visualization parameters included maximum-spanning forest edge reduction with strongest edges per node, VOS-style community layouts for distance-based networks, and ForceAtlas2 LinLog for co-authorship networks [E022–E026]. Temporal overlay mapping was applied to keyword networks to visualize conceptual evolution [E065].

### Bradford Zoning

Source concentration was analyzed using Bradford's law, dividing ranked sources by cumulative document thirds. Records without source names were excluded from zoning [E019].

## Results

### Performance Structure: Growth, Productivity, and Impact

The research domain spans 2015 to 2022 [E004], exhibiting remarkable growth dynamics. Annual output increased from 2 publications in 2015 to 72 in 2022, representing a compound annual growth rate of 66.85% [E006][E007]. The growth trajectory shows three distinct phases: an emergence phase (2015–2017) with modest output (2–13 publications), an acceleration phase (2018–2020) where output more than doubled from 33 to 52 publications, and a consolidation phase (2021–2022) where output reached 48 and 72 publications respectively [E007]. The slight decline from 52 to 48 publications between 2020 and 2021 represents the only year-over-year decrease in the series [E007].

The corpus consists entirely of journal articles (100%), with no review or systematic review documents identified [E014]. This composition suggests a field dominated by primary research contributions rather than synthetic reviews, consistent with an emerging domain where experimental methodologies are being actively developed.

Citation impact reveals a highly skewed distribution characteristic of emerging fields. The mean citation count of 72.09 substantially exceeds the median of 32.00, indicating that a small number of highly cited works drive the average upward [E015][E017]. The 90th percentile reaches 192 citations, while the 95th percentile extends to 292.1 citations [E017]. The maximum citation count of 1,436 belongs to a 2022 publication on *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis and emerging therapeutics [E017][E018]. Notably, 35 works (13.51%) have received zero citations [E016], a proportion that must be interpreted in light of the field's recency, as 72 publications appeared in 2022 alone [E005].

The most highly cited works reveal the thematic core of the field. The top-cited publication (1,436 citations) addresses *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis, virulence factors, and emerging therapeutics including CRISPR-Cas systems and outer membrane vesicles [E018][E027]. The second-ranked work (651 citations) describes efficient RNA drug delivery using red blood cell extracellular vesicles, demonstrating both antisense oligonucleotide and Cas9 mRNA delivery [E018][E028]. The third-ranked publication (611 citations) presents exosome-liposome hybrid nanoparticles for CRISPR/Cas9 delivery in mesenchymal stem cells [E018][E029]. Other highly cited works address EV-based drug delivery systems considering cell source (589 citations) [E030], circular RNA targeting strategies (569 citations) [E031], and nanoparticle delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 (359 citations) [E032]. This citation hierarchy reveals that works integrating EV biology with therapeutic delivery, particularly CRISPR/Cas9 applications, dominate the impact landscape.

### Social Structure: Authors, Institutions, and Collaboration Networks

Author productivity is concentrated, with Xiaohui Chen ranking first with 14 publications—more than triple the output of the next most productive authors [E010][E011]. A cohort of nine additional researchers each contributed 4 publications: Chenghui Liu, Huilan Li, Kan Ouyang, Li Duan, Limei Xu, Shan Xing, Wei Ren, Xiao Xu, Yi He, and Yujie Liang [E011]. The co-authorship network, constructed from 131 eligible authors with minimum occurrence of 2, reveals 10 distinct collaboration clusters [E023][E060]. The network displays 149 edges among 60 displayed nodes, with the largest cluster centered on Huilan Li, Shan Xing, and Yi He (each with weighted degree 30.0), while Xiaohui Chen anchors a separate cluster with weighted degree 29.0 [E023]. The ForceAtlas2 layout achieved a layout score of 0.061 with zero overlap, indicating well-separated collaboration communities [E060].

Institutional productivity shows a tripartite leadership structure, with Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University each contributing 7 publications [E012][E013]. Nanjing Medical University and Shaanxi Normal University follow with 5 publications each, while University of Oxford, Air Force Medical University, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Guangzhou Medical University, Nanjing University, National Institutes of Health, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and Shenzhen Second People's Hospital each contributed 4 publications [E013]. The institution collaboration network, constructed from 134 eligible institutions with minimum occurrence of 2, displays 10 clusters with 137 edges among 71 displayed nodes [E025][E061]. Harvard University anchors cluster 7 with weighted degree 20.0, while a dense Chinese institutional network emerges in cluster 1, connecting Guangzhou Medical University (weighted degree 18.0), Sun Yat-sen University (12.0), Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (12.0), and Fu Wai Hospital (12.0) [E025]. The VOS-style layout achieved a within-between distance ratio of 0.403, indicating moderate community separation [E061].

Source productivity is led by the *International Journal of Molecular Sciences* with 9 publications, followed by the *Journal of Extracellular Vesicles* (7 publications), *Nature Communications* and *The FASEB Journal* (6 each), and *Analytical Chemistry* and *Cancers* (5 each) [E008][E009]. # Anonymous Bibliometric Report

## Structured Abstract

**Background:** The intersection of extracellular vesicle (EV) biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology represents a rapidly evolving frontier in therapeutic delivery. A systematic bibliometric characterization of this domain is needed to map its intellectual structure.

**Methods:** A corpus of 259 unique works was acquired from a single bibliographic source via cursor pagination until exhaustion [E001, E002]. Metadata completeness was assessed across 11 fields [E003]. Descriptive analyses of annual output, leading sources, authors, and institutions, and citation impact were performed. Science mapping included Bradford zoning, keyword temporal trends, a three-field plot, and five network analyses (coauthorship, institution collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, cocitation, bibliographic coupling) using association-strength normalization and Louvain community detection [E019–E026].

**Results:** The corpus spans 2015–2022, with annual output peaking at 72 works in 2022 and a compound annual growth rate of 66.85% [E004–E007]. *International Journal of Molecular Sciences* is the most prolific source (9 publications) [E008]. Xiaohui Chen is the most productive author (14 publications) [E010]. Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University lead institutional output (7 publications each) [E012, E013]. The mean citation count is 72.09, with a median of 32.00; 13.51% of works are uncited [E015, E016]. The keyword co-occurrence network reveals five thematic clusters, with “Biology,” “Gene,” and “Cell biology” as central nodes [E026].

**Conclusion:** The field exhibits rapid, sustained growth and is concentrated in a core of high-impact journals and institutions. The thematic structure, dominated by EV-mediated CRISPR delivery, is visualized through complementary network maps. All findings are bounded by source-dependent metadata and citation windows.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Background and Rationale
The convergence of extracellular vesicle research and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing has generated a distinct, interdisciplinary literature. A bibliometric approach is warranted to quantify its growth, identify key actors, and map its conceptual structure [E067].

### 1.2 Objectives
This report aims to: (i) characterize the volume and growth trajectory of the corpus [E001, E004–E007]; (ii) identify the most productive sources, authors, and institutions [E008–E013]; (iii) analyze citation impact and distribution [E015–E018]; and (iv) reveal the intellectual and collaborative networks underpinning the field [E019–E026].

## 2. Reproducible Methods

### 2.1 Data Acquisition and Corpus Assembly
Records were retrieved from a single bibliographic source. Cursor pagination continued until the source returned no next cursor, yielding 259 unique source records, matching the source-reported total of 259 [E002]. Deterministic exact deduplication on canonical work identifiers confirmed a final corpus of 259 unique works [E001].

### 2.2 Metadata Quality Assessment
Field completeness was calculated as the percentage of non-null canonical values for 11 metadata fields. Coverage was 100% for title, publication date, year, source ID, document type, cited-by count, and reference count; 99.61% for language; 97.3% for DOI; 96.14% for publisher; and 84.56% for abstract [E003].

### 2.3 Analytical Procedures

#### 2.3.1 Descriptive and Productivity Analyses
Annual output was whole-counted by publication year [E007]. Compound annual growth rate (CAGR) was calculated from the first and last non-zero annual counts [E006]. Top sources, authors, and institutions were ranked by whole-counted publications [E008–E013]. Document types were tabulated from source-supplied classifications [E014].

#### 2.3.2 Citation Analysis
Citation counts are source- and retrieval-date-dependent [E015]. Descriptive statistics (mean, median, percentiles, maximum) and the zero-citation share were computed [E015–E017]. The 15 most-cited documents were identified by descending citation count [E018].

#### 2.3.3 Science Mapping and Network Analysis
Bradford’s law of scattering was applied to sources with known names, dividing them into three zones by cumulative document thirds [E019]. Keyword temporal dynamics were tracked for the 15 most frequent normalized keywords [E020]. A three-field plot (author–source–keyword) was constructed using whole-counted links [E021].

Five networks were constructed using a candidate-first association-strength method [E022–E026, E069]. Candidate nodes were selected by minimum occurrence thresholds. Edges were normalized using association strength (c_ij / (w_i * w_j)), where c_ij is the number of co-occurrences and w_i, w_j are the total occurrences of items i and j. Community detection was performed via the Louvain algorithm, with small clusters merged [E070]. Networks were visualized with edge reduction (maximum-spanning forest plus strongest edges per node) and layout optimization (VOS-style or ForceAtlas2 LinLog, best of multiple restarts) [E022–E026, E060–E066]. The specific networks are: bibliographic coupling (minimum 5 references per document, minimum 2 shared references) [E022, E064]; coauthorship (minimum 2 occurrences) [E023, E060]; cocitation (minimum 3 occurrences) [E024, E063]; institution collaboration (minimum 2 occurrences) [E025, E061]; and keyword co-occurrence (minimum 5 occurrences) [E026, E062, E065, E066].

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Corpus Overview and Growth
The corpus comprises 259 unique works published between 2015 and 2022 [E001, E004]. Annual output grew from 2 publications in 2015 to a peak of 72 in 2022, with a CAGR of 66.85% [E005–E007]. A year-over-year decline of 4 publications was observed only in 2021 [E007]. Figure 1 illustrates this trajectory [E051].

### 3.2 Leading Sources, Authors, and Institutions
All 259 works are classified as “article” by the source; no documents are classified as reviews or systematic reviews [E014]. The 15 most productive sources are led by *International Journal of Molecular Sciences* (9 publications), followed by *Journal of Extracellular Vesicles* (7) and *Nature Communications* (6) [E008, E009, E052]. Bradford zoning reveals a core Zone 1 of 23 sources accounting for 85 documents [E019, E058].

Xiaohui Chen is the most prolific author with 14 publications, substantially ahead of the next-ranked authors (4 publications each) [E010, E011, E053]. Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University jointly lead institutional output with 7 publications each [E012, E013, E054].

### 3.3 Citation Impact
The mean citation count is 72.09, and the median is 32.00, indicating a right-skewed distribution [E015, E017]. The maximum citation count is 1,436 [E017]. A total of 35 works (13.51%) have zero source-reported citations [E016]. The most-cited document is a 2022 review on *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis (1,436 citations) [E018, E027]. Its high citation count and tangential relationship to the EV-CRISPR intersection suggest it may represent a highly cited work captured by the search strategy rather than a core document of the field.

### 3.4 Thematic Structure and Networks
The keyword co-occurrence network contains 72 displayed nodes and 200 edges, partitioned into 5 Louvain clusters [E026, E062]. The highest-weighted nodes are “Biology,” “Gene,” and “Cell biology” [E026]. The temporal overlay indicates a mean keyword year range of 2018.57 to 2020.89 [E065]. The density visualization appears to highlight “Biology” and “Microvesicles” as high-density regions, consistent with their high occurrence in the network [E026, E066]. Keyword trends show consistent annual increases for “Biology” and “Gene” [E020, E059].

The bibliographic coupling network (72 nodes, 211 edges, 8 clusters) identifies “Gene Editing by Extracellular Vesicles” as the most central document by weighted degree [E022, E064]. The coauthorship network (60 nodes, 149 edges, 10 clusters) reveals two large clusters: one centered on Huilan Li and Shan Xing, and another, separate cluster containing the most prolific author, Xiaohui Chen [E023, E060]. The institution collaboration network (71 nodes, 137 edges, 10 clusters) shows Harvard University as the highest-degree node, with a distinct Chinese institutional cluster centered on Guangzhou Medical University and Sun Yat-sen University [E025, E061]. The cocitation network (72 nodes, 203 edges, 7 clusters) is structured around highly cited references identified by OpenAlex IDs [E024, E063]. The three-field plot confirms Xiaohui Chen’s central role, linking to “Analytical Chemistry” and multiple keywords including “Biology,” “Gene,” “Microvesicles,” “Biochemistry,” and “Chemistry” [E021].

## 4. Discussion

### 4.1 Principal Findings
This analysis documents a rapidly expanding research domain, with a 66.85% CAGR and a 36-fold increase in annual output from 2015 to 2022 [E006, E007]. The field is concentrated in a Bradford core of 23 journals, with *International Journal of Molecular Sciences* as the leading venue [E008, E019]. Author productivity is highly skewed, with Xiaohui Chen contributing to 5.4% of the corpus [E010, E001]. Institutional leadership is shared among Harvard University and two Chinese universities, reflecting a trans-Pacific research axis [E012, E013].

The citation distribution is typical of a fast-growing field: a high mean relative to the median, a long tail of highly cited works, and a non-trivial uncited share attributable to recent publication dates [E015–E017]. The most-cited work, a 2022 review on *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis, is not topically central to EV-mediated CRISPR delivery and may represent a highly cited work captured by the search strategy rather than a core document of the field [E018, E027].

The network analyses reveal a coherent thematic structure. The keyword co-occurrence map’s five clusters, anchored by “Biology” and “Gene,” suggest a core focus on the biological mechanisms and genetic engineering applications of EVs [E026]. The bibliographic coupling network’s central document on “Gene Editing by Extracellular Vesicles” confirms the integrative nature of the field [E022]. The coauthorship and institution collaboration networks indicate strong intra-institutional and intra-national clustering, with emerging cross-cluster links [E023, E025].

### 4.2 Interpretation in Context
The observed growth aligns with broader trends in nanomedicine and gene therapy research. The prominence of journals such as *Journal of Extracellular Vesicles* and *Nature Communications* underscores the field’s positioning at the intersection of specialized EV biology and high-impact multidisciplinary science [E009]. The dual leadership of U.S. and Chinese institutions mirrors the global competitive landscape in biotechnology [E013]. The thematic emphasis on delivery systems, as evidenced by dominant keywords like “Microvesicles” and “Gene,” and by top-cited documents on EV-mediated CRISPR delivery, indicates that translational application is a primary driver of research activity [E018, E020, E026].

## 5. Limitations

### 5.1 Data Source and Coverage
All findings are contingent on the single bibliographic source used. Metadata completeness, while high for core fields, is lower for abstracts (84.56%) and publisher (96.14%), which may affect text-based analyses [E003]. Document-type labels inherit source classification practices [E014].

### 5.2 Temporal and Citation Constraints
The final year (2022) may be incomplete if retrieval occurred before year-end [E005]. Citation counts are retrieval-date-dependent and favor older publications due to longer citation windows [E015, E016]. The CAGR of 66.85% is an endpoint measure; the observed year-over-year decline in 2021 confirms the growth is not monotonic [E006, E007].

### 5.3 Analytical Constraints
Productivity rankings are descriptive and must not be interpreted as measures of research quality or causal influence [E009, E011, E013]. Network centrality metrics describe the constructed corpus and parameterization, not substantive importance [E022–E026]. All abstract-based inferences are limited to source-supplied metadata and cannot support claims requiring full-text inspection [E027–E050]. Bradford zoning excludes records without a source name [E019].

## 6. Conclusion
This bibliometric analysis maps a dynamic, rapidly growing research domain at the nexus of extracellular vesicle biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. The corpus of 259 articles (2015–2022) is characterized by exponential growth, concentration in a core of specialized and high-impact journals, and a distinct thematic structure centered on therapeutic delivery applications. Key contributors include Xiaohui Chen as the leading author and a trans-Pacific institutional axis led by Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen Universities. The network visualizations provide a reproducible, multi-perspective map of the field’s intellectual and collaborative landscape. These findings offer a structured baseline for researchers, funders, and policymakers to understand the field’s evolution and identify emerging fronts, while acknowledging the inherent constraints of source-dependent bibliometric data.

value.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) is a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen that infects patients with cystic fibrosis, burn wounds, immunodeficiency, chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder (COPD), cancer, and severe infection requiring ventilation, such as COVID-19. P. aeruginosa is also a widely-used model bacterium for all biological areas. In addition to continued, intense efforts in understanding bacterial pathogenesis of P. aeruginosa including virulence factors (LPS, quorum sensing, two-component systems, 6 type secretion systems, outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), CRISPR-Cas and their regulation), rapid progress has been made in further studying host-pathogen interaction, particularly host immune networks involving autophagy, inflammasome, non-coding RNAs, cGAS, etc. Furthermore, numerous technologic advances, such as bioinformatics, metabolomics, scRNA-seq, nanoparticles, drug screening, and phage therapy, have been used to improve our understanding of P. aeruginosa pathogenesis and host defense. Nevertheless, much remains to be uncovered about interactions between P. aeruginosa and host immune responses, including mechanisms of drug resistance by known or unannotated bacterial virulence factors as well as mammalian cell signaling pathways. The widespread use of antibiotics and the slow development of effective antimicrobials present daunting challenges and necessitate new theoretical and practical platforms to screen and develop mechanism-tested novel drugs to treat intractable infections, especially those caused by multi-drug resistance strains. Benefited from has advancing in research tools and technology, dissecting this pathogen's feature has entered into molecular and mechanistic details as well as dynamic and holistic views. Herein, we comprehensively review the progress and discuss the current status of P. aeruginosa biophysical traits, behaviors, virulence factors, invasive regulators, and host defense patterns against its infection, which point out new directions for future investigation and add to the design of novel and/or alternative therapeutics to combat this clinically significant pathogen.

Release from bone marrow, in response to chemokine elevation, has been considered their source, but chemokine levels peak up to 24 h after injury, and after neutrophil elevation. value.abstract: CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing is a very promising avenue for the treatment of a variety of genetic diseases. However, it is still very challenging to encapsulate CRISPR/Cas9 machinery for delivery. Protein N-myristoylation is an irreversible co/post-translational modification that results in the covalent attachment of the myristoyl-group to the N-terminus of a target protein. It serves as an anchor for a protein to associate with the cell membrane and determines its intracellular trafficking and activity. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are secreted vesicles that mediate cell-cell communication. In this study, we demonstrate that myristoylated proteins were preferentially encapsulated into EVs. The octapeptide derived from the leading sequence of the N-terminus of Src kinase was a favourable substrate for N-myristoyltransferase 1, the enzyme that catalyzes myristoylation. The fusion of the octapeptide onto the N-terminus of Cas9 promoted the myristoylation and encapsulation of Cas9 into EVs. Encapsulation of Cas9 and sgRNA-eGFP inside EVs was confirmed using protease digestion assays. Additionally, to increase the transfection potential, VSV-G was introduced into the EVs. The encapsulated Cas9 in EVs accounted for 0.7% of total EV protein. Importantly, the EVs coated with VSV-G encapsulating Cas9/sgRNA-eGFP showed up to 42% eGFP knock out efficiency with limited off-target effects in recipient cells. Our study provides a novel approach to encapsulate CRISPR/Cas9 protein and sgRNA into EVs. This strategy may open an effective avenue to utilize EVs as vehicles to deliver CRISPR/Cas9 for genome-editing-based gene therapy.

value.abstract: Molecular diagnostics devoted to discover and monitor new biomarkers is gaining increasing attention in clinical diagnosis. In this work, a programmable DNA-fueled electrochemical analysis strategy is designed for the determination of an emerging biomarker in lung cancer, PD-L1-expressing exosomes. Specifically, PD-L1-expressing exosomes are first enriched onto magnetic beads functionalized with PD-L1 antibody and are able to interact with cholesterol-modified hairpin templates. Then, programmable DNA synthesis starts from the hairpin template-triggered primer exchange reaction and generates a large number of extension products to activate the trans-cleavage activity of CRISPR-Cas12a. After that, CRISPR-Cas12a-catalyzed random cleavage boosts the degradation of methylene blue-labeled signaling strands, so electro-active methylene blue molecules can be enriched onto a cucurbit[7]uril-modified electrode for quantitative determination. Our method demonstrates high sensitivity and specificity toward electrochemical analysis of PD-L1-expressing exosomes in the range from 10 3 to 10 9 particles mL –1 with a low detection limit of 708 particles mL –1 . When applied to clinical samples, our method reveals an elevated level of circulating PD-L1-expressing exosomes in lung cancer patients, especially for those at the advanced stages. Therefore, our method may provide new insight into liquid biopsy for better implementation of immunotherapy in lung cancer in the future.
